nodes.name: Weekly, Monday 04:00
nodes.notes: Fires in GENERIC_TIMEZONE. Unset, this runs at an hour nobody chose.

nodes.name: Fetch the acts
nodes.notes: Re-downloads the consolidated acts and prints the manifest digest. Cheap: two documents, and the fetcher writes only when the text actually differs.

nodes.name: Did the corpus change?
nodes.notes: Static workflow data holds the last digest, so a week with no change is a no-op rather than a full re-index and a re-run of every stored check.

nodes.name: Re-index
nodes.notes: Idempotent by construction. A clause's point id is its deterministic chunk_id, derived from (regulation, article, paragraph, source_version), so a re-index overwrites the same points rather than duplicating them — and every citation already stored in Postgres still resolves. No --reset: dropping the collection is only correct when the chunking itself changed.

nodes.name: Which checks are affected?
nodes.notes: Compares the text behind each stored citation against the freshly indexed corpus and returns only the passed checks whose cited clauses actually changed. Derived from the corpus, never from a list this workflow keeps — a stored worklist would drift the moment a run failed halfway.

nodes.name: Re-run the check
nodes.notes: http://api:8000 — the compose service name. Re-running is keyed on the original job id, and the API refuses if the source document is no longer retained, so a re-run cannot invent a report from a document nobody has.
